statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH (yellow). NQ trades at 29,338.50, down 111.00 points or 0.38%, after fading its recovery high at 29,384.25 back toward a 29,308.50 session low that has now held for roughly two hours. ES marked a marginal new low at 7,660.25 without confirmation from NQ. One failed retracement lifts Tail from 20 to 21, while the held low, the contained 186.75-point overnight range and conflicting index internals keep it well inside the watch band. Stress stays high at 72 on a 5.025% US 10-year and WTI above 103.
recommendation: Tail at 21 maps to WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The one-point increase from last hour records a single piece of adverse structure: the 76-point bounce off the low was given back and ES printed a marginal new session low at 7,660.25. Three separate observations hold the score down. NQ did not confirm that new low, its 29,308.50 floor has survived about two hours of testing, and the full overnight range is 186.75 points or 0.64%, which is orderly rather than violent. Under this framework a functioning retracement is direct evidence against the pathological no-retracement path, and a single failed bounce is not the repeated extension that the elevated band requires. The rate and energy backdrop is the dominant stress input rather than a path input: the 10-year reached 5.025%, its highest since 2007, WTI trades at 103.24 up 1.82%, and the two-day Federal Reserve meeting opens today with the decision not due until 18:00 UTC on Wednesday, beyond this forecast horizon. Index internals conflict rather than align, with the semiconductor complex heavily negative while Communication Services gained 2.68% and megacaps split four up and four down, and cash VIX at 17.10 is not corroborating a stress event. The declared danger window is 13:00 to 15:00 UTC around the US cash open, which remains the first deeply liquid test of the broken 29,426.75 shelf. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection are unaffected by the mapped state.
headline: NQ fades its bounce to 29,338.50 but the 29,308.50 low holds for a second hour as ES prints a marginal new low - Tail edges to 21 with Stress high at 72 on a 5.025% 10-year
body:
The development of this hour is a failed retracement that did not become an extension. NQ gave back the bounce that took it to 29,384.25 an hour ago and now trades at 29,338.50, down 111.00 points or 0.38% against a 29,449.50 prior close, with a second independent source showing 29,334.50 on the same structure. The session low remains 29,308.50 and has not been retested successfully, leaving it intact for roughly two hours. ES is the weaker of the two, trading at 7,662.50 after marking a marginal new low at 7,660.25, below the 7,663.00 low that stood an hour ago. That divergence matters: the framework requires both index futures pinned to extremes before treating the structure as one-way, and NQ is declining to confirm.

The macro backdrop is genuinely difficult and is the reason Stress remains high at 72. The US 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.025%, the highest since 2007, having first crossed 5% on Monday for the first time since October 2023. The drivers reported are an oil-led revival of inflation concern, heavy debt issuance including corporate financing of record AI capital spending, and fiscal deterioration. WTI trades at 103.24, up 1.82% on the day within a 101.83 to 103.49 range. The tension in this setup is that long-end yields are making multi-decade highs while the Federal Reserve is expected to cut to 3.75% on Wednesday.

The equity driver is separate and sector-specific. Reporting confirms that industry calls to slow frontier AI model development, including from Anthropic's chief executive, triggered Monday's semiconductor selloff, with the chip complex punished harder than the hyperscalers because it is most exposed to a slowdown in capability improvement. Latest-session moves show ARM down 9.74%, INTC down 5.59%, MU down 5.25%, AVGO down 4.77% and AMD down 4.40%. Against that, Communication Services gained 2.68% with GOOGL up 3.22% and META up 2.71%, and megacaps split four positive and four negative. This is rotation inside the index, not aligned index-level liquidation, and conflicting internals raise Stress rather than Tail.

Two further observations restrain the score. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Monday at 29,127.16, down 0.82%, but only after dipping to 28,867.67 and recovering more than 259 points into the close, which is a mean-reversion outcome rather than a trend-day outcome. And cash VIX at 17.10 is not corroborating a stress regime, with futures volatility up only 1.48%. Aligned amplifiers are present in yields, oil and semiconductors, but the observed price path, the index internals and the volatility complex all argue against the persistent no-retracement structure that the elevated band measures.

The dominant mode is mixed. The forecast holds the low twenties through the European morning, marks the 09:00 UTC window that produced Monday's chip-led leg, eases into the pre-US lull, and rises to a 24 peak across the declared 13:00 to 15:00 UTC danger window covering the US cash open and the first full cash hour. It is deliberately held below the block threshold there because no opening structure has been observed and Monday's equivalent session recovered. The 17:00 UTC 20-year bond auction is treated as a genuine checkpoint given the long-end repricing. Conditional risk then decays through the US close into the Asian session, reaching a cycle low of 15, before rebuilding into the European pre-open on Federal Reserve decision day.

lookbackSummary: The published record covers all 24 preceding clock hours. Tail ran 21 to 26 through Monday's European and US morning, peaking at 26 twice around the chip-led decline and the US cash open, then decayed steadily through the US afternoon to 15 and 14 overnight as price discovery turned orderly. It re-accelerated to 24 at 05:00 UTC when NQ broke its 29,426.75 floor with both index futures pinned to session extremes, and eased to 20 at 06:00 UTC when a 76-point retracement resolved that structure. Stress stayed in the 65 to 79 band throughout, reflecting a rate and energy backdrop that never reset. Confidence held between 86 and 89 on continuously available price-path evidence.
outlookSummary: The conditional path holds 21 for the remainder of this hour, lifts to 22 for the European cash open and holds 22 across the 09:00 UTC window that produced Monday's chip-led leg. It eases to 21 and 20 through the European late morning and the pre-US lull, returns to 21 for the 12:15 and 12:30 UTC releases, and rises to a 24 peak across the declared 13:00 to 15:00 UTC danger window covering the US cash open and the first full cash hour. That peak is held at the top of the watch band rather than in the block band because no opening structure has been observed and Monday's cash session recovered from its low. It eases to 22 and 21 through the US afternoon, ticks to 22 for the 17:00 UTC 20-year bond auction, and to 22 again for the closing hour. After the 20:00 UTC cash close conditional risk decays through 20, 18, 17 and 16 into the Asian session, bottoming at 15 in the Asian mid-session, before rebuilding through 16, 17, 18 and 19 into the European pre-open on Federal Reserve decision day. Stress tracks the same shape between 74 and 64 without leaving the elevated-to-high range, because the 5.025% 10-year and WTI above 103 do not reset overnight.
